facts.text: The town was renamed Weiner in 1881 when the Louis and Southwestern Railroad built a station, honoring a St. Louis railroad official.
A post office named West Prairie opened in 1874, and by 1884, it was renamed Weiner; the town incorporated on December 2, 1907.
Between 1870 and 1880, the West Prairie area saw a notable influx of new settlers, including several families of German origin drawn by reports of fertile land.
Originally featuring a prairie landscape surrounded by forests, the topography around Weiner consists of rolling to flat plains that were largely cleared for farmland by the mid-20th century.
Weiner is part of the Jonesboro, Arkansas Metropolitan Statistical Area, reflecting its regional ties.
